channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Between Seasons: Black & White Photography from City to Sea · Photo Art Pavilion
item.description: An annual juried, in-person black-and-white photography exhibition at the Southampton Cultural Center on the eastern end of Long Island, run by Photo Art Pavilion — the US art-photography marketplace and community founded by Joanne Henig and Jessica Lempin, who also founded Long Island Photo Gallery. Exactly 40 photographs are selected from the entries in a blind jury, with Henig and Lempin jurying and no artist names visible to them; selection runs on centre of interest, composition, focus and exposure, story, lighting, creativity and uniqueness rather than on one house style. All styles are welcome and the call is explicit that it does not care what the picture was made with — DSLR, point-and-shoot, smartphone or film — only that the work is black and white, the photographer's own and in keeping with the city-to-sea theme. The cash awards are $150 for first place, $125 for second, $100 for third and $35 for each honourable mention, announced live at the artists' reception rather than in advance, and the selected 40 are also published in an online gallery kept on PhotoArtPavilion.com in perpetuity. Entry is $37 for the first five images and $3 for each image after that, up to ten, with one submission per photographer; files are JPEGs at 72 dpi with the longest edge at least 1200 pixels, under 5 MB, free of watermarks or branding, and only the title is needed at upload. Note before you enter that this is a physical show on Long Island: work is delivered or installed on 1 March 2027, the exhibition runs 2–27 March, and every exhibiting artist is expected to attend the reception and awards in person on 27 March at noon Eastern, with pickup at 2:30 the same day. Southampton Cultural Center takes a 25% commission on any sale made during the show, and Photo Art Pavilion passes purchase enquiries straight to the artist on the artist's own terms. Open to photographers 18 and over, internationally, and notifications go out by the end of 15 January 2027. — Deadline: January 11, 2027. Fee: $37 for up to 5 images ($3 per additional image). Prize: $150 + $125 + $100 + Exhibition.

item.title: Résidence Incertitude 2027 · Freelens / IRIT
item.description: Freelens — the French photographers' association recognised as being of public utility — and IRIT, the CNRS computer-science research institute in Toulouse, run this annual photographic residency on the theme of uncertainty in science. It is conceived and directed by Cédric Févotte, CNRS research director at IRIT, with artistic direction by Céline Pévrier of sun/sun éditions. One photographer is invited to build a body of work across four to six weeks at IRIT, taken in one to three stays in the first half of 2027, with weekly check-ins and introductions to researchers whose expertise fits the project; applicants are asked not to approach IRIT scientists before applying. The laureate receives €6,000 inclusive of charges and VAT (of which €1,000 is the rights assignment for the presentation, exhibition and book), paid 40% on signature, 30% after the work with the publisher and 30% after the work with the exhibition venue, plus up to €3,000 for travel, accommodation in Toulouse and technical costs. On top of that sit a dedicated envelope for sun/sun éditions to publish a book of the project and a production budget for the resulting exhibition at Galerie Le Château d'Eau, the photography venue in Toulouse, alongside a public presentation at IRIT. The call is open to professional photographers — photographic authors or visual artists using the medium — French and international, who are fluent in French; the residency is open to pluridisciplinary projects that weave writing, sound or other modes into the photography. Applying is free but the règlement requires every applicant to join Freelens for €15 by card or PayPal, a membership that also covers every other Freelens event, grant and prize. The dossier is a single PDF of at most 20 pages and 10 MB: an intent note of up to five pages, a portfolio of up to fifteen, the proposed residency calendar, a one-page CV, a short bio and the completed application form, filed through the Google form by midnight on 30 November 2026. A pre-jury of Freelens board members and the residency's direction shortlists five candidates for a video interview before the final jury, which the règlement fixes at five seats — Févotte, Pévrier, Freelens president Sophie Knittel, one figure from the photography sector and one from scientific research. Interviews are scheduled for 17 December, subject to change, with the result announced "le 23 décembre 2027 au plus tard" as the page prints it. The 2026 laureate was Éléa-Jeanne Schmitter, and the residency carries the French Ministry of Culture's Bicentenaire de la Photographie label through 30 September 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €15 Freelens membership (application itself free). Prize: €6,000 + 4–6 week residency + €3,000 expenses + Book publication + Exhibition.

item.title: The Photography Foundation Awards 2026
item.description: The Photography Foundation is the UK's largest photography-specific charity, and its annual awards are run as a fundraising project for that charity's work with emerging creatives. Every entrant gets one free image entry; each additional image is £8 and those fees are treated as donations. There are seven categories — Black and White (sponsored by Black+White Photography Magazine), Landscapes, urban and natural (Manfrotto), Music, Portraits & People (Capture One), Social Documentary (LIMI London), Street Photography and Wedding Photography — and entrants may submit as many images in as many categories as they wish. One overall winner receives £2,000 from Leica towards a new or ongoing photographic project. The winner and runner-up of the Black and White category are published in Black+White Photography Magazine; the Portraits & People winner gets a year of Capture One and a one-day pass to shoot at the Foundation's studio; the Landscapes winner receives a Manfrotto ONE Photo Alu tripod with XPRO ball head. Winners, runners-up and highly commended entrants are all exhibited at the annual Awards Exhibition, hosted by Leica London in 2025 and 2026 and by The Photobook Cafe before that. Judging is strictly anonymous — entrant details are stripped from the images and the eighteen judges vote independently of one another. The awards are explicitly open to amateurs as well as professionals, with entries accepted from all countries, and images must have been taken during 2026. The entry form does not sell single extra images: its dropdown offers one free entry, a 3-image pack at £16, 5 images at £32 or 10 at £72 — exactly £8 for every image past the free one, though the smallest paid outlay is £16 — alongside an optional £5–£100 donation that is not required to enter. The clause that bars AI also bars composites: entries must be authentic camera works, and "composite images, digital artwork, or images that incorporate elements not captured by the photographer through a camera lens are not eligible", with standard post-production allowed and the original RAW file open to request. An image that has already won the title of Overall Winner of another photographic competition cannot be entered, and files are JPEG or TIFF between 800KB and 5MB. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free for one image (£8 per additional image). Prize: £2,000 + magazine publication + exhibition.

item.title: Palermo Takeover 2027
item.description: Palermo Galerie is handing over its programme. From June to December 2027 the Stuttgart project space is opening its rooms to artists, collectives and curatorial teams and inviting independent proposals for exhibitions, performances, screenings, discussions and other experimental formats — “Your programme. Your ideas.” The space itself is the story: Palermo occupies the vacant former Schwabenbräu-Passage in Stuttgart-Bad Cannstatt, repurposed as a temporary gallery and project room for contemporary art until the owner modernises or demolishes the site, and it is run by Kunstverein Dialekt e.V., which has been supported by the City of Stuttgart's Kulturamt since 2005, with the gallery project additionally backed by the city's Liegenschaftsamt and Wirtschaftsförderung, the Bad Cannstatt district council, Dinkelacker Schwabenbräu, Werkstatthaus and Stuttgarter Jugendhaus gGmbH. The association states its position plainly: exhibitions are developed through cooperative and solidaristic processes, the focus is not the economic valorisation of artistic practice but the recognition of its intrinsic value and social dimension, and artists are treated not as entrepreneurial agents producing for a market segment but as producers of work that exists independently of exchange-value logic. It also writes the possibility of failure into its ethos as a productive force that enables experimentation. Be clear about what is and is not on offer, because the call is. What you get: rent-free space, existing technical equipment by arrangement and subject to availability, and 70% of food and drink revenue for your team with 30% going to the association. A total of €5,000 in funding has been applied for — and the call states that support will only be available if that funding is approved, so it cannot be counted on. What you carry: financing, organisation, publicity and any additional event permits required. This is a venue and a platform rather than a funded commission, which makes it a fit for a photographer or collective that already has a show in mind and wants a real room and an engaged audience rather than a prize. Applications run from 1 November 2026 to 15 January 2027 and consist of your concept, team information, a preliminary programme schedule, a funding strategy and work samples or links, sent by email. The call is published in German and English and sets no restriction on where applicants are based. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Rent-free exhibition space + 70% of bar and food revenue.

item.title: PhotoForum Open Call 2026 — Photobooks and Online Exhibitions
item.description: PhotoForum Inc. — which has been publishing books and magazines since Photo-Forum magazine launched in 1974 and is funded primarily by its members — opens one call covering two strands of its 2027 programme, with a single email submission for both. The first is its print publishing programme: PhotoForum produces two publications a year and is looking for engaging recent photographic projects to be developed as its upcoming photobooks. The terms are stated plainly and are worth reading in full before applying. Each publication is issued as a limited edition with the majority sent to subscribed members; all publishing costs are covered by PhotoForum; copyright of the images remains with the artist; and the artists will not receive any payment but will receive five copies of the book. For a photographer with a resolved body of work and no publisher, a fully funded limited-edition photobook that costs nothing to enter is a substantial offer — but it is a publication, not a fee. The second strand is a series of online exhibitions planned for 2027, showcasing a wide selection of photographic work alongside newly commissioned writing, and these are open to individual photographers as well as partnerships, collaborations and collectives. Here there is money: selected photographers receive a modest fee for online publication, and publication will likely fall between March and November 2027. PhotoForum frames the commissioned writing as essential — it sees the involvement of writers as the way to create discourse around photographic artworks and widen the audience for both photography and the writing about it, which is also why its online exhibitions sit alongside a long-running essays and reviews programme rather than standing alone. Submissions for either strand are a PDF accompanied by a short artist statement of about 200 words and a bio. Decisions are made by PhotoForum's Publications and Online Subcommittees against three published criteria: do we love the work; is the proposed project cohesive and relatively resolved in its scope; and is the project consistent with the organisation's vision of continuing a strong legacy of significant photographic publications in Aotearoa New Zealand. The one hard gate is geography — submissions are welcomed from photographers based in Aotearoa New Zealand. The deadline is 5 pm on 23 November 2026. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + Modest payment for online exhibitions.

item.title: The Eyes are Bigger Than the Stomach: Food and Contemporary Art · Indy Art Center
item.description: A national juried exhibition at the Indy Art Center built on a subject the organiser calls universal: “There are few things so universal and central to the human experience as food. It has shaped cultures, customs, geography, politics and much more across centuries.” The question put to artists is how we reflect on food through contemporary art in 2026 — including the contemporary edges of it, which the call names explicitly: food scarcity, factory farming, climate change. The brief is deliberately open on medium: this is a call “open to any artist working within the theme or concept of food with no specified medium required”, and the Art Center states that all artworks which connect to food in some way, through media, concept or theme, will be considered, with jurors approaching the theme under an encompassing definition covering both traditional techniques and contemporary methods of making. For a photographer that is a wide door — documentary work on agriculture and the food supply, still life, studio and alternative-process work all sit inside it — and the eligibility clause confirms it: entries are open to artists 18 or older residing in the United States, working in any media, with work made within the last two years that has not been shown at the Art Center before. Entry is two works for $35 with $5 for each additional piece up to a maximum of fifteen, and awards are cash: $300 Best in Show, $150 Best in 2D, $150 Best in 3D and two honourable mentions of $100 each. The exhibition is a long one — it opens 5 April 2027 and closes 13 June, with the reception on 16 April, 5 to 8 pm — and it runs in six galleries at an institution that mounts more than a dozen contemporary art exhibitions a year. Practical terms worth knowing before applying: all work may be offered for sale and the Art Center retains a 35% commission on sales; the artist pays shipping, insurance in transit and return shipping, and work must arrive in a reusable container by 21 March 2027 (hand delivery opens 20 February); work must not exceed 250 pounds or ten feet in any direction; and installation artists are asked to make contact before applying. The deadline is 17 February 2027 with notifications by end of day on the 19th. — Deadline: February 17, 2027. Fee: $35 (two works) + $5 per additional work. Prize: $300 + $150 ×2 + $100 ×2 + Exhibition.

item.title: Solo Exhibition December 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: All About Photo runs a Solo Exhibition every month, and December 2026 is the next open slot. The selected photographer gets the whole month — 1 to 31 December 2026 — across the site's home page, competition gallery and photography exhibition directory, plus an exclusive interview, a dedicated portfolio page holding 20 images in the Photographers Directory, and a permanent place in the showroom archive after the month ends. The organiser also commits to specific press: a special-edition newsletter announcing the exhibition, promotion across its Instagram, Facebook and Twitter accounts, and guaranteed publication on Bored Panda, Visura and Photophiles Magazine, with past winners having been picked up by The Times UK, National Geographic España, The Eye of Photography and Digital Camera World. Sales during the exhibition are commission-free — the photographer keeps the full price. The juror for this cycle is Olga Karlovac, a self-taught photographer based in Zagreb whose trilogy “before winter”, “the disarray” and “escape” sold out its first edition and whose work has run in Black+White Photography and the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. The theme is open and every genre is invited — photojournalism, street, fine art, landscape, portraiture — from professionals and enthusiasts alike, anywhere in the world. What matters is cohesion: the entry is 6 to 14 images for a flat $45, and the organiser is explicit that only cohesive projects or portfolios will be published as a Solo Exhibition, so a set of unrelated strong frames is the wrong submission here. Two practical notes. This is an online-only exhibition — there is no physical venue and no cash prize; what is awarded is a month of placement, an interview and the press package above, so judge the $45 against visibility rather than against an award. And entry runs through an account on All About Photo's own site: the “Enter Competition” button redirects to the site's sign-in and back to this page, so there is no separate submission portal to bookmark. The deadline is Tuesday 17 November 2026, two weeks before the exhibition opens. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PhotoSpiva 2027 · Spiva Center for the Arts
item.description: PhotoSpiva is the longest-running photographic competition of its kind in the United States — Spiva Center for the Arts in Joplin, Missouri has run it every year since 1977, and the 2027 edition follows the 50th. The founders' brief still governs it: “present an exhibition of excellence in photography, celebrating the scope and vigorous activity of today's contemporary photographers”, and co-founder Jim Mueller's note that “we have intentionally avoided any categorization of either photographers or their work” is why there is still no theme and no category. Any photographic process qualifies — traditional, digital or photo-based mixed media — provided the work is two-dimensional, original, and has never been exhibited at Spiva before; three-dimensional work is not eligible. Entry is open to any amateur or professional photographer in the United States or its territories, with no age floor and no career-stage bar. Selected work hangs 20 March – 29 May 2027 in Spiva's galleries in the Harry M. Cornell Arts & Entertainment Complex, with the opening reception and awards on Friday 19 March 2027, 5:30–7:30 pm. The award ladder is cash and substantial for a $40 entry: $1,000 first, $750 second, $500 third, three $150 Merit Awards and three $100 Honorable Mentions — $3,000 in all. A new juror is invited each year from among, in the organiser's words, the nation's most respected photographers and curators; the 2027 jurors are Louviere+Vanessa, the collaborative duo whose work crosses photography, film, painting and printmaking, named on the call's own CaFE record — the organiser's own page has not caught up and still carries the 2026 juror, Dan Winters. Know the fee structure before you start: the $40 buys exactly five images and you must enter five, no fewer — the prospectus explicitly allows entering the same photograph five times if you do not have five — and each image beyond the fifth is $10. All images must go in one application; files are JPEG in RGB, with roughly 1600 pixels on the long edge given as a guideline rather than a rule. Acceptance or declination is sent by email by 27 January 2027. Two costs land only if you are selected. Accepted work must be printed, mounted on a rigid backing and matted — and may not be framed; Spiva partners with a local print house that offers accepted artists discounted printing and matting, though you may prepare your own to its specifications. Shipping and insurance both ways are the artist's responsibility, and the Center's “all risk” policy covers only theft and fire. Sale is optional, and the split on anything sold is 60% to the artist. Entering grants Spiva the right to reproduce an entry for publicity tied to this or future exhibitions. Two things to check before you click through. The entry window opens on 6 November 2026 at midnight Central, so the CaFE record carries no apply button until then — at the time of listing its page showed the prospectus but not the “Apply on CaFE” route a live sibling record carries. And the organiser's own page contradicts itself: its “How to Participate” block is stale and still prints the 2026 cycle's “Begin entering on November 7, 2025” and “Deadline is Jan 5, 2026”, while its “terms and conditions” link opens the 2026 prospectus. The binding window is the one in the “PhotoSpiva 2027 Key Dates” block and in the 2027 prospectus: 6 November 2026 to 4 January 2027 at 11:59 pm Central. The competition is presented by Freeman Health System with support from the Missouri Arts Council. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: $40 (5 images) + $10 each additional. Prize: $1,000 + $750 + $500 + 3×$150 + 3×$100 + Exhibition.

item.title: New Year Commission 2027 · Photoworks
item.description: Photoworks, a registered charity that describes itself as the only organisation with a national remit for photography in England, is commissioning one photographer or lens-based artist to make a single new image marking the start of 2027. The organisation has no physical venue — the Brighton address on this listing is its postal address, and the commission runs entirely online. The brief is deliberately loose and playful: a non-conventional image that indicates the beginning of a new year, with room to experiment rather than illustrate. The commission pays a £500 fee and comes with an Instagram takeover of the Photoworks account in January 2027. The finished image travels further than most single-image commissions: Photoworks shares it across its social platforms, sends it to a mailing list that it describes as including curators, editors, artists and industry professionals, and prints it as a postcard that ships with every Photoworks shop order through 2027. Entry is free and no images are uploaded — the form carries no file field at all — but the application is more than a link: it asks for your name and email, a portfolio link (website or Instagram), and a written answer to “How would you approach creating an image for this commission?”. Everything after that, from location and age range to ethnicity, gender and caring responsibilities, is optional equal-opportunities monitoring, and applying adds you to the Photoworks mailing list. The call is explicitly international: the organisation says it looks forward to hearing from applicants wherever they are in the world, the form's location question offers “Outside the UK, please state country”, and the organiser's standing page for this commission says it goes to an artist at any stage in their career. Three things to know before applying. No selection panel is named and no notification date is published, so there is no stated timetable between the 5 December deadline and the January takeover. The deadline is printed as “Deadline 5 December.” with no time of day, and this organiser does publish one when it has one — its previous Photography+ open call closed at 9:00 am GMT — so treat 5 December as the last safe day rather than a full one. And note the route: the page's web address still carries last year's slug while the page itself is headed New Year Commission 2027, and the only 2026 inside the call block is the credit line on Ning Cheng's previous commission. — Deadline: December 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £500 + Publication.

item.title: The Meridian Award — Cycle III
item.description: An independent international award granting a $2,000 fully unrestricted cash prize to one contemporary artist working in any medium, with $200 to each of two finalists. Founded in New York City, it is open to all artists aged 18 and over worldwide with no restriction on nationality, location, education or professional status, and there is no theme — portfolios are judged on artistic merit, clarity of vision, coherence of the work presented and the strength of a distinct artistic perspective. Photography is named in the award's own discipline list alongside painting, drawing, digital art, sculpture, print-based media, textile-based media, performance, sound art, video art and interdisciplinary practice; short and feature-length films are the only stated exclusion. Winner and both finalists are invited to an individual interview published on the award's website and Instagram. Apply through the award's own form with a name, a biography (150 words), an artist statement (250 words), a work description and up to five files, images and video links combined, each image under 2MB and named for its artwork; a separate portfolio PDF is not required. The fee is $30, non-refundable, and no fee waivers are offered. Two things to weigh. The jurors are described as invited contemporary-art professionals but are not publicly named, which the organiser states is deliberate. And this third cycle is twice as rich as the last — Cycle II paid $1,000 at a $25 fee — while the award's own About page still reads "The second cycle of The Meridian Award is now officially open for applications"; it is the FAQ that labels the January 15, 2027 deadline as Cycle III. The payout record is real: the inaugural 2026 cycle went to Brooklyn sculptor Wen Liu, a 2026 AIM Fellow at the Bronx Museum with fellowships from Yaddo, MacDowell and Bogliasco, with painter Matt Bollinger and interdisciplinary artist Andrius Alvarez-Backus as finalists. That is also the only result the award has published so far; the cycle that closed on October 18, 2026 has not been announced. Artists keep full copyright; by applying they agree their materials may be used for the award's promotional and editorial posts. The winner is announced in February 2027. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: $2,000 + two $200 finalist awards.

item.title: Drone Photo Awards 2027 · Siena Awards
item.description: Siena Awards' aerial photography contest returns for 2027 with nine categories and a prize package that helps cover the stay in Italy. The rules open with the eligibility line — “Drone Photo Awards competition is open to professional and amateur photographers”. Seven single-shot categories are published (Wedding, Nature, People, Urban, Animals, Abstract and Sport), alongside a Videos category and a Series category, where “You may enter from 5 to 9 images” on “a set of images that are presented together on the same theme, edited in the same style, and with a common link.” Six of the single-shot briefs define the work as “captured from the sky” and Abstract as “Aerial photography”, though neither the Videos nor the Series brief states an aerial requirement of its own. Entry is free for one image; beyond that the rules' Entry Fees table reads “3 images (including the free one) € 30”, “Each additional image € 10”, and € 35 for a Series or a Videos entry, with “no refunds provided” once paid. The entrant “with the highest scoring image will be endowed the title of ‘Drone Photographer of the Year’” and there is also a winner in each category; the overall winner receives “€ 500,00 worth of photography equipment”, the “Pangea Prize” crystal trophy, and “a fixed fee of 400 euros to assist with accommodation expenses for two overnight stays in Siena during the Awards Ceremony weekend”, reimbursed after the winners are announced. Two conditions attach to the awards: the trophies and parchments “will only be given to winners attending the Awards Ceremony”, and equipment “not collected during the ceremony will be the responsibility of the winners”. Winners are honoured on stage at the ceremony in Siena, and “the winning images will be showcased in Siena at the ‘Above Us Only Sky’ exhibition during 2 months”, with advertising in the international press. Photographers keep their copyright — “Siena Awards recognizes you retain full ownership of the copyright in each photograph that you have submitted” — and grant only promotional use of entered images. AI is barred outright: the rules prohibit AI generation software “for the creation or enhancement of images”, including AI-generated elements added to camera-captured frames and generative fill used to extend an image beyond its original boundaries. No 2027 juror is named — entries are “reviewed and pre-screened by our editors and an international group of industry professionals”, then judged by “our international jury”, and the award's jury route serves only the roster of previous editions. Entries opened on 11 October 2026 and close on 1 June 2027. — Deadline: June 1, 2027. Fee: Free (1 image); €30/3, €10 each extra; €35 Series/Videos. Prize: €500 gear + €400 accommodation + exhibition.

item.title: Rooted + Rising · Pierro Gallery
item.description: A free, no-commission municipal gallery show for Black artists, with photography named in the gallery's own accepted media. The Pierro Gallery of South Orange describes Rooted + Rising as bringing “together local and regional Black artists whose work reflects the many ways history, culture, creativity, pride, resilience, and activism continue to shape contemporary expression. These artists carry stories and traditions forward while making something entirely their own, reminding us that culture is not static—it grows, changes, and finds new ways to speak.” Eligibility is stated in one line on the call: “Emerging and established local and regional artists are welcome to apply” — the gallery sets no county or state boundary anywhere on the call or in its guidelines, and its standing exhibitions policy reads that artists are “featured with special sensitivity to regional artists but without precluding consideration of work by any visual artist”, so the geography is a preference rather than a published bar. Up to three works may be submitted with title, medium, dimensions, year and price; a short artist statement and bio are asked for only from artists who are selected, who are also sent a Release of Liability form to sign. Images should be kept under 10 MB, and the gallery states it “cannot respond to inquiries or provide feedback on individual pieces” because of submission volume. Photography is explicitly welcome — the gallery's FAQ lists “paintings, sculptures, photography and mixed media” — and work needing glass or Plexiglass must meet standard framing guidelines (flat wood or metal, white, black or natural preferred, no more than 1″ wide from the front, no decorative frames unless part of the artwork), with unconventionally presented works on paper accepted if the presentation is professional. There is no submission fee: “We do not charge a submission fee. We believe in providing artists with an opportunity to showcase their work without financial barriers.” Sales are allowed and the gallery takes nothing from them — it “operates on a non-commission basis” and asks only for a voluntary donation. Founded in 1994 and named for the late artist and arts advocate Lennie Pierro, the gallery is run by South Orange's Department of Recreation and Cultural Affairs at the Baird Community Center. Artists are notified the week of 14 December 2026, drop-off is mid-January, and the exhibition runs 4 February to 4 April 2027. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: story · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery's next juried online show takes narrative as its subject — "story: adventure, tale, narrative, myth, drama, fable, saga, fiction, novel, fantasy…." — and the gallery makes good on the theme itself: co-director Kevin Tully, writing as Frank Cincinnatus, "will write a short tale to go along with the Juror and Director Award images", and the prospectus prints a sample of his fiction in full. Tully is also the juror; he is a photographer, designer, writer and artist who "has curated and installed hundreds of exhibitions for the gallery" and has juried for All About Photo, Analogue Forever, Dodho Magazine, the International Photography Hall of Fame and Critical Mass. The call is open and unlimited: "The competition is open to all photographers both professional and amateur working in all photographic mediums and styles. International entries are welcomed", at $40 for the first five images and $5 for each additional one, with "no limit to the number of images you may submit"; work previously shown in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible. Jurying is blind, with images renamed and numbered. Up to 47 images are selected for an online exhibition that is permanently archived, featured image by image on the gallery's Facebook and Instagram, discussed in a recorded GalleryTalk, listed for sale in the gallery's online store and published in a purchasable exhibition catalogue; 27 of the 47 also go into "The 27", a hardbound fine art book. The Juror and Director Awards each bring "a online solo exhibition, 'The 27' exhibition book and feature story on the gallery blog", and the Visitors Award, decided by Instagram likes, pays $100. Photographers submitting 13 or more images get a free 30-minute review with the gallery directors; fewer than 13 costs $20 for the same. Photographers keep full rights, the gallery takes 30% of any sale, and a sold print may be shipped by the artist or printed by the gallery. The exhibition runs 8 January to 18 February 2027. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images + $5 each. Prize: $100 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: PhotoWings x Photoville Educator Exhibition Grant 2027
item.description: The tenth edition of a grant that puts school students’ photographs into a major public festival. Photoville, with PhotoWings, invites middle and high school educators to propose an exhibition of their students’ work for the 2027 Photoville Festival, which spreads across Brooklyn Bridge Park and all five boroughs. Six educators are selected, and each receives "Curatorial, design, printing, and logistical support from the Photoville team", "A public exhibition of their students’ work as part of the 2027 Photoville Festival" and "A $500 cash grant". READ BOTH OF PHOTOVILLE’S OWN PAGES, BECAUSE THEY STATE ELIGIBILITY DIFFERENTLY. The festival homepage gives only a school-level bar: "This program is ONLY open to Middle and High School Educators who work directly with students. School Administrators and Elementary and College programs will not be considered." The grant’s own info page — the route that homepage links as its "info page" — adds a condition the homepage never mentions, and softens the geography: "This grant is open to all middle and high school educators who have participated in a Photoville Education program in the past. Please note that New York City based schools will be given priority in the selection process." So New York is a stated priority rather than a bar, and the grant’s own published recipient list runs past the five boroughs: alongside schools in the Bronx, Park Slope and Staten Island it names the Issaquah High School Photo Club and the all-Tribal "Our Community Record Two Eagle River School, Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes". The prior-participation clause, though, is stated flatly, so an educator new to Photoville should ask before building a proposal. The grant builds on "9 years of collaboration with educators to develop lesson plans inspired by photography projects", and what it funds is the exhibition that comes out of teaching one: educators "implement a photo-based lesson from the Photoville Educator Resource library in their classroom and produce a culminating exhibition of student work". Photoville notes that "for the past 8 years we have seen a vastly dynamic array of students’ work". Proposals go through Photoville’s own submission form, which closes "January 4, 2027 at 11:59pm ET"; the festival’s separate artist call for proposals closes earlier, on 22 December 2026. Photoville Festival is supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 + exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Call for Entries — Detroit · Subjectively Objective
item.description: The photobook publisher Subjectively Objective is opening "a new series of exhibitions at our soon to be expanded Detroit area gallery space" and taking submissions of up to ten images. There is no theme: "This is an open call with no specific theme, as this will allow us the greatest ability to create a variety of interesting exhibitions. Our primary focus is on contemporary landscape and documentary photography, but even if your work falls outside of that, please don't hold back from submitting." Work not placed in one of these shows is still considered for the publisher's other channels — "our Substack Features, Instagram Features, and Mini and Monthly Monograph Magazines" — and returning contributors are explicitly invited back. READ THE COST STRUCTURE BEFORE YOU APPLY: the $10 submission fee is only the entry, and "if selected, the artist will be responsible for an exhibition fee that covers the cost of producing their exhibition print(s), the opening, and promoting the physical exhibition." You pick the largest print size you want to be considered for — you remain eligible for smaller ones — and that choice sets the bill if you are taken: $30 per image for a small print (about 15x12 inches), $45 medium, $65 large (25x20), $90 XL (30x24), $150 XXL (40x32), $300 for a full eight-foot wall, $350–600 for a wall of larger prints, and $600+ for multiple walls, the last being "for those open to the possibility of participation in a small group show or even a solo exhibition". Printing is done in house by founder Noah Waldeck, who "will be using the same expert techniques he uses to make museum quality prints for his custom lab clients", and after the show he will send your print on if you cover shipping. The submission fee itself is waivable: "If you can't afford the submission fee, please contact me and we'll figure something out." Instructions arrive as a downloadable PDF once the fee is paid. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $10 + $30–$600+ exhibition fee if selected. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Photoville Festival 2027 — Call for Proposals
item.description: The 16th annual Photoville returns to New York for "three weeks of free public art, exhibitions, and community programming in Brooklyn Bridge Park and across all five boroughs", and the call is as wide as the festival: "We are looking for ALL types of photographic and lens-based work. We welcome everything from documentary and photojournalism, to fine art, sports, and conceptual work. Alternative processes such as photo collage, tintypes, and cyanotypes are all welcome too!" The festival wants "global narratives, local histories, studio portraiture, street photography, collaborative archives, community-driven projects, and interdisciplinary approaches" and work on "immigration, healthcare, education, racial inequality, climate change, social justice, incarceration, women's rights, youth and intergenerational stories, police reform, housing, joy". Because the shows stand in public parks, it asks you to "avoid images that may be shocking — particularly images of nudity, sexual intercourse, drug use, or violence". There are three applications — two for exhibitions (open-air structures sited across the five boroughs, and the festival's signature shipping containers in Brooklyn Bridge Park) and one for public programming, a talk, workshop or interactive experience; you may submit more than one proposal, and Photoville steers unsponsored artists to the open-air route because container slots are few and costly. The economics are the point: "Independent artists selected for the festival do not pay exhibition costs. Photoville covers all design, production and installation expenses to ensure equitable participation." For a selected artist or artist-led collective with no institutional support or sponsorship, Photoville states it will "cover the cost of printing, exhibition structures, installation, public liability insurance, publicity, and will pay a modest artist honorarium", the amount varying with the number of artists supported and the scope of the project. Artists, non-profits and commercial entities that DO arrive with sponsorship are asked for a contribution instead, assessed per proposal and quoted at $5,000–$40,000 for open-air and $12,000–$40,000 for a container. Eligibility is deliberately unrestricted: "All photo-based artists (and collectives, organizations, and companies representing this work) are welcome to apply! There is no limit or prerequisite regarding artist age, professional qualifications, or time period the work was made in." Selected artists get a one-to-one virtual meeting with the Photoville team and then work with it to produce the exhibition. Photoville is supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs with the City Council, with Brooklyn Bridge Park and NYC Parks as host partners. — Deadline: December 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + payment.

item.title: CUPOTY CHALLENGE 2026: Close to Home
item.description: The themed contest that runs alongside the annual Close-up Photographer of the Year competition, and for 2026 the theme was chosen by vote — "the CUPOTY community has voted in record numbers on the theme and Close to Home came out on top!" The brief is "overlooked wonders in your home, garden or on your doorstep": "close-up, macro and micro photographs taken in a home and its immediate surroundings: the home's rooms, outbuildings (such as sheds, garages and greenhouses), garden, balcony, doorstep or the street directly outside", your own home or that of family or friends. The organisers suggest "frost on a window, a spider in the shed, a mushroom in the garden, the patterns in a soap bubble, a bee in a flower, moss on the step, a leaf brought in from the garden and photographed on the kitchen table", and they rule out "public gardens, parks, allotments, nature reserves, holiday accommodation and commercial premises". Open to "all professional and amateur photographers of any age and nationality" — entrants of 17 or under may enter with a parent or guardian making the payment — and there is no limit on how many entries you buy, nor any date limit on when the pictures were taken. Process is wide open: "any type of camera may be used to capture an image for the Competition, including a mobile phone, scanner or camera trap", and a scan or photograph of "an image made directly on light-sensitive material, such as a photogram, cyanotype or lumen print" counts. Judging is anonymous (each file is given an identifying number) by "a panel of photography experts". The overall winner takes £300, second £125 and third £75, with winner and finalist pictures shown in an online winners gallery and "included in any book or exhibition of CUPOTY". Entrants keep copyright: "CUPOTY respects your rights and does not claim copyright for pictures you submit", while shortlisted and winning images are licensed for competition promotion for five years. Two dates matter: paid entry closes 30 November 2026 "wherever you live in the world", after which you can no longer pay, but "images for entry can continue to be sent to CUPOTY up to 7th December". Shortlist in March 2027, winners in April 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: £11 for 1 picture / £16 for 3 (£10/£14 to 8 Nov). Prize: £300 / £125 / £75.

item.title: Repurpose: The Art of Upcycling · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: A national juried exhibition at Artlink in Fort Wayne for work made with upcycled material — "through use of found objects, reuse of materials, or repurposing of old artworks", in the gallery's words, upcycling being "the art of taking discarded materials and elevating them into a renewed existence of higher quality, greater value, or increased utility." The theme is about material rather than medium: the prospectus states "Any media is eligible, there is no size limit and any artist 18+ residing in the United States is eligible", and the eligibility block repeats "Media accepted: all" — which leaves the door open to photographers working with salvaged negatives and prints, found imagery, cameraless and alternative processes, or printing on reclaimed surfaces. Entry is $12 per work with a $12 fee for each additional piece, up to ten, one application per artist through CaFE. The show runs 18 February to 14 March 2027 and accepted work must reach the gallery by 7 February. The artist pays shipping both ways and must enclose a return label; framing is not required, but shipped work that is framed has to use plexiglass rather than glass; sales carry a 35% gallery commission, paid by cheque after the show closes. Artlink insures work on its walls but not in transit, and damage from the artist's own packing is not covered. Artlink is a 501(c)3 nonprofit contemporary gallery in the Auer Center for Arts & Culture in downtown Fort Wayne, funded in part by Arts United and the Indiana Arts Commission. — Deadline: January 11, 2027. Fee: $12 per entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: A Wild Life: The Art of Animals · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: A national juried exhibition at Artlink's gallery in Fort Wayne for artwork inspired by animals — in the gallery's own framing, "from direct depictions celebrating the beauty, fierceness, or fragility of animal-kind, to conceptual works exploring human impact, endangerment, and loss of habitat." The call is explicitly all-media and names photography and video alongside painting, sculpture, ceramics, glass, jewellery, fibre, drawing and installation; the prospectus adds "Media accepted: all" and sets no size limit. Entry is $12 per work, with a $12 fee for each additional piece and a maximum of ten; applications are made once per artist through CaFE. The show runs 18 February to 14 March 2027 with an opening reception on Thursday 18 February, 5–8pm, and accepted work must reach the gallery by 7 February. Practical conditions worth pricing before entering: the artist pays shipping both ways and must enclose a return label, framing is not required but any shipped work that is framed must use plexiglass rather than glass, and sales carry a 35% gallery commission, paid out by cheque after the show closes. Artlink insures work while it is on the walls but not in transit, and damage caused by the artist's own packing is not covered. Open to artists 18 or over resident in the United States. Artlink is a 501(c)3 nonprofit contemporary gallery in the Auer Center for Arts & Culture in downtown Fort Wayne, funded in part by Arts United and the Indiana Arts Commission. — Deadline: January 11, 2027. Fee: $12 per entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Booooooom Photo Awards
item.description: Booooooom's annual photography awards, run by the long-standing art and photography platform founded by Jeff Hamada. Five category winners are named across Portrait, Nature, Street, Student and Series — the last of these new for 2026 and built for cohesive bodies of work rather than single frames. Each category winner receives $1,000, a WANDRD camera bag (the PRVKE 21L for Portrait and Series, the ROGUE for Nature, Street and Student), an interview and feature on Booooooom, promotion across its social channels and a place on the awards mini-site. Three shortlisted photographers additionally receive a Manfrotto ONE Photo aluminium tripod with XPRO ball head, and sixteen participants drawn from across the whole entry pool — not only the winners — receive a hardcover photo book designed and printed by foto foto. A shortlist of twenty and a longlist of two hundred are published on the awards mini-site and across Booooooom's social channels. The jury is Katy Hundertmark, managing editor of Foam Magazine; Pat O'Rourke, founder and curator of Rental Magazine; the photographer Jennilee Marigomen; and Elena Rebecca Rivolta, editor-in-chief of PHROOM. Entry is free for a single image in one category; $25 at the early-bird rate covers up to ten images, which may span several projects, in one category; and an Awards Pass covers unlimited images across every category. Work must have been made in 2025 or 2026. The Student category is open to anyone who was enrolled in a school of any kind when the work was made, and students may enter the same work in the other categories as well. — Deadline: December 9, 2026. Fee: Free (1 image); $25 early-bird category, $50–$70 pass. Prize: 5 × $1,000 + equipment + publication feature.

item.title: Color · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed group exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe for work in which colour itself does the talking — the next call in the gallery's rolling monthly programme, following Darkness and Black and White on the same board. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, a fine art photographer whose work has been exhibited and published internationally; 26 images are selected for the gallery walls. The gallery covers the whole cost of presentation — one exhibition-quality print on Luster paper, custom framing in the gallery's signature 24×24 inch black museum-quality frames, and matting from its collection of precut white mats, resized by the gallery's team without cropping the original composition. Artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG between 500KB and 5MB with the longest side at 4,500 pixels. The exhibition runs March 5 to 26 with an opening reception on March 5; the year is not printed on the page, but March 5 2027 is the first Friday of that month, which is the gallery's own stated scheduling convention, and the January 28 2027 deadline with its two-week notification window leaves no room for a 2026 show. After the show the physical print is archived in the gallery's flat files, photographers retain all rights to their images, and any sale splits 50/50 between gallery and photographer. Acceptance is emailed within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due within two days of that email. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10, non-refundable. — Deadline: January 28, 2027. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Kranj Foto Fest Open Call for Exhibitions 2027
item.description: The exhibition open call for the seventh edition of Kranj Foto Fest, a Slovenian festival of contemporary photography founded in 2021 and run by the non-profit Zavod Photo Dialogue. Up to thirteen projects are selected. Twelve of them enter group exhibitions with the festival covering the full production cost of the work — printing and installation — plus three nights' accommodation during opening week, 26–29 August 2027. From those, one grand prize winner receives a solo exhibition with production costs covered, a €1,000 cash prize and up to €400 in travel support to attend the festival. There is no thematic or technical restriction, but the photographs must form a coherent story, series or project. Applicants may be photographers, visual artists or visual storytellers working individually, in duos or as collectives, from anywhere in the world, and the terms set a floor of 18 years. Each project is 10 to 20 JPG images with a minimum of 1,500 pixels on the longest edge, submitted at a resolution suitable for printing, with a project description of up to 2,500 characters and a bio of up to 1,500; text may be in Slovene or English, and English is recommended. Up to two projects may be entered, at €12 for one and €16 for both. Artists who have exhibited at the festival before may reapply only with a different project; festival staff, sponsors, jury members and their relatives may not apply. The jury is Maryam Wahid of Tasweer Photo Biennale, Amin Yousefi of Photoworks and Photography+, Edda Fahrenhorst of horizonte zingst and Yeast Photo Festival, Peter Rauch of the University of Ljubljana's Academy of Fine Arts and Design, and festival founding director Fernanda Prado Verčič. Judging takes place in January 2027 and results are emailed in February. The 2027 festival runs 26 August to 26 September in Kranj. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: €12 (€16 for two projects). Prize: Solo exhibition + €1,000 + €400 travel.

item.title: Arty Rat Magazine Open Call — December 2026
item.description: Arty Rat is an independent art journal run from Vienna by curator Oleksandr Dyvnich, showcasing contemporary visual art, illustration and “bold creative voices from around the world”; the open call page addresses itself to “artists and photographers”. This is the next rolling cycle after the 1 November one, at the same standing call page. Submission is free, open worldwide to applicants 18 or older, and up to six works may be entered as JPG or PNG — either through the form on the call page, or by pasting a Google Drive or Dropbox link into it, or by emailing the files to the journal. Selected artists receive a free digital copy of the magazine as a PDF, photographs of their printed magazine pages and a feature on the journal's Instagram; two selected artists have their work on the magazine covers, and one selected artist takes part free of charge in a group exhibition at The Names Gallery in Vienna — a show the call page still dates only as “the end of August” with no year. A participation fee applies only if the work is selected, and the organiser lists the options openly: €35 for publication in the magazine, €65 for publication plus an artist's page on the website with biography, statement and photographs of works, €100 for a curatorial review covering magazine and website, and €100 for the Vienna exhibition. The fee is non-refundable. The most recent issue, Issue 5, was published in September 2026. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free (€35–€100 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: BINGO February 2027 — Cheek to Cheek · Candela Photographic Arts
item.description: The second run of Candela's “give two, get one” small-print open call, and the first with a theme. Candela Photographic Arts — the Richmond, Virginia gallery and independent photobook publisher that became a 501(c)(3) in 2026 after fifteen years as Candela Books + Gallery — asks for “interpretations of touch and fresh takes on the photographic tradition of the nude – particularly, the beloved bottom”. Cheek to Cheek “explores intimacy through touch, gesture and form”: hugs, kisses, caresses, the spaces between, or a favourite derrière, with unconventional, experimental and playful readings of every form of love explicitly welcome. The gallery adds its own disclaimer — keep the work “thoughtful, playful, and/or conceptual”, because Candela “isn't interested in nude imagery that feels exploitative or needlessly vulgar”. Fourteen small photographic works are selected and hang from 8 January to 13 February 2027, alongside Candela's January/February solo exhibitions, before a ticketed Valentine's bingo fundraiser on 13 February at which every framed print on view goes home with a winner. Selected artists send two unframed editions of their image: the first is an in-kind donation that Candela frames and mats at its own cost and gives away on Bingo Day, the second enters a randomised swap that mails another participant's print back to the artist, postage covered by the gallery. Submission is free — “there is no fee to submit to the Bingo show” — and opened on 3 November 2026. Up to three photographic prints may be entered; each must exist in at least two editions (variant editions accepted) and measure no more than 12 inches on the longest side. Submissions take 1–3 JPEGs, the artist's contact details, each work's title, year, medium, dimensions and edition information, and a short statement or bio. Accepted artists are announced on 1 December 2026 and must ship both prints to the gallery by 15 December. Candela encourages alternative processes, tiny prints, variant editions, and work from “side quests, one-off projects, proofs, or works-in-progress” as readily as finished bodies of work — and is candid that the exhibition “is philanthropic and community-focused in nature and may not be a great fit for artists looking for big sales opportunities”. The gallery names no juror. Artists after the gallery's flagship juried show are pointed at UnBound16!, whose own open call runs 5 January to 12 February 2027. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + print swap.

item.title: Prix Roger Pic 2027 · LaScam
item.description: LaScam — the Société civile des auteurs multimédia, the French authors' society for multimedia work — has run the Prix Roger Pic since 1993, named for the humanist photographer, director and copyright campaigner who instigated it, and awards it each year to the author of a photographic portfolio that documents the real and questions the human with singularity. This is the 35th edition, run in partnership with Fisheye magazine. The award is €4,000, and with it comes €1,240 (gross, or excluding tax) in droits de monstration — an exhibition fee paid to the winner for showing the awarded portfolio in LaScam's own gallery in Paris, where Vincent Gouriou's Les ombres claires, the 2026 winner, hangs from 5 October 2026 to 19 February 2027. LaScam states the prize is meant for photographers whose talent has not yet had the recognition it deserves, and the roll of laureates is the best argument for entering: Vincent Gouriou (2026), Véronique de Viguerie (2025), Corentin Fohlen (2024), Mário Macilau (2023), Baudouin Mouanda (2022), Alexis Vettoretti (2021), Sandra Reinflet (2020), Tomas van Houtryve and Denis Dailleux (2019), Laura El-Tantawy (2018), Michael Ackerman (2009), Christian Lutz (2011) and Martin Kollar (2005). Entry is free and there is no membership requirement — work is read from photographers who do not belong to LaScam — but the call is for professional photographers over 18, of French or any other nationality. The portfolio must be unpublished and must not have won any award (contest, festival, book, slideshow) before the date of registration; one portfolio per author per year, and a different one each year; only complete bodies of work are considered, never unfinished projects. Note the language condition, which is easy to miss and decides whether you can apply: accompanying texts must be written or translated into French. The online file is a portfolio of 20 photographs (JPG, 1–5 MB each, at least 2000 pixels on the long side, with IPTC title, description and photographer's name), a title and caption of up to 300 characters for each photograph, a 900-character summary plus a presentation and letter of intent (PDF, two A4 portrait pages maximum), and a biography of the author and any co-authors (same format). Two stages follow: the authors of LaScam's commission des images fixes draw up a pre-selection of ten portfolios, then a jury renewed every year — commission members, the president of the LaScam-Vélasquez association, and outside figures from photography, where possible including a previous laureate — picks the winner from those ten, with registrations processed December to February and the pre-selection and jury sitting March to April. Two conditions sit in the regulations rather than the call text, and registering online is what accepts them: photographs entirely generated by AI are not accepted, and every candidate grants LaScam free use of up to two of their photographs to promote the prize, worldwide for a year and tacitly renewed unless cancelled two months before the year ends. The deposit page runs 4–30 November 2026 and opens at 08:00 Paris time on the first day. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €4,000 + €1,240 exhibition rights + Exhibition.

item.title: Artistic Calendar 2027 · iTravelPoetry
item.description: iTravelPoetry — a Greek publisher and cultural venue in Chalandri, in the Athens suburbs, whose photography programme runs the Beyond Borders open call and its own festival — is assembling the Artistic Calendar 2027 (Καλλιτεχνικό Ημερολόγιο 2027), a collective edition that turns a year of days into a printed anthology of reader and contributor work. Four entry categories are named and photography is one of them: a poem of up to 30 lines, a text or short story of up to 500 words, a painting or other visual work, or a photograph. The theme is free. Each creator may enter one or two works — €13 for one, €20 for two, plus shipping, and each option includes one copy of the finished book; extra copies are €10 each. Work in another art form, or work over the line or word limit, is priced separately on request. Be clear about what the fee buys: the call names no jury and describes no selection stage for the four listed categories, and its own words are an invitation to participate and a “confirmation of your participation”, so the €13 buys a place in the edition rather than a shot at one — the organiser's framing is that creators carry none of the production cost, and with a €10 copy included the real entry cost is a few euros plus postage. The edition is a printed A5 book, black-and-white throughout (worth weighing if you work in colour), carries an ISBN and a BookPoint registration, and is launched at the publisher's own cultural space at Irakleiou 6, Chalandri. Under Greek copyright law 2121/1993 the copyright stays with the creator and the exploitation rights sit with the publisher, but the works are explicitly not bound editorially to iTravelPoetry, so you may use the same work in other editions of your own or in other collections. Entry is through the form on the call page, which takes the finished file (JPG, PNG, DOC, DOCX or PDF) and asks for a postal address for the copy; payment is by bank transfer to an account sent with the confirmation of your participation, with any bank charges on the sender. The form also makes you pick one of four promotion options before it will submit — a photo and CV added (€10 + VAT), a written interview on the publisher's site (€20 + VAT), a professional video feature (€200 + VAT), or “no promotion, calendar entry only” — and that last one is free, so none of it belongs to the entry price. The call is published only in Greek and its form asks for your name in Greek characters, so a non-Greek-speaking photographer should expect to write to the publisher before entering. Submit the final file: the organiser states that no changes are accepted after submission. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: €13 (1 work) / €20 (2 works) + postage. Prize: Publication + contributor copy.

item.title: Snow Much to See 2026
item.description:
Snow Much to See is an international photography contest devoted to snow, ice and cold, now in its second edition. It is run by the photographer Giandra De Castro and is part of the programme of Images & Neige, a festival founded in Cluses, in the Haute-Savoie Alps, by the photographer Frédéric Boiteux, which describes itself as the only photography festival in Europe entirely devoted to that theme. The festival's 17th edition runs from 22 to 24 January 2027. Every photograph must have an identifiable link with snow, ice or cold.
Entries compete in 11 categories, each open to single images and to series of 3 to 20 photographs: snowy or icy landscapes; scenes of winter life; urban environments shaped by cold or snow; winter sports and leisure; wildlife and plants in cold environments; the human, social or environmental consequences of cold; poetry and reverie; minimalism, graphics and abstraction; macro and close-up; smartphone; and drone. The last three are defined by technique and accept any subject. An entrant may submit up to 60 single images and several series, and the same photograph can be entered both ways, in which case it is judged and charged twice.
Seven winners are exhibited at the festival, with production paid for by the organisers. Four series winners each have three photographs chosen by the jury, printed in a 40 × 60 format with pigment inks on Hahnemühle paper and framed in wooden box frames. Three single-image winners, a first, second and third prize, are printed in 30 × 45. The prints stay with the organisers. Each category also awards one single-image prize and one series prize. No prize carries cash. Winners, category winners and jury favourites appear in the exhibition catalogue with the jury's written analysis.
Free photographs exist in only two categories, Sport and Urban. In each, the first single image and the first two photographs of a series kept in that category are free, so two single images can be entered at no cost. A series needs at least three photographs, so a series always costs something. Paid photographs from both formats are added together and charged once: €5 for up to 3, €10 for up to 10, €15 for up to 20, and €2 for each one beyond 20. From €5, the entrant receives a PDF of the catalogue with every photograph commented. From €25, which is 25 paid photographs — the organiser advertises this tier as "31 photos", counting the 6 free ones — the entry also gets a one-page written review, sent on 11 January 2027. Fees are not refunded unless the contest is cancelled.
Files are JPEGs of at least 2,000 pixels on the long side, with no watermark, signature or frame, and judging is anonymous. Usual editing is allowed, including panoramas, exposure blending and focus stacking from the entrant's own shots. Photomontages and images generated or altered by artificial intelligence are not accepted, and the original file may be requested. The jury is Giandra De Castro (president), Frédéric Boiteux and three people from the City of Cluses, which hosts the exhibition: Françoise Guillen, Priyam Nursimhulu and Manon Canale. Entrants keep their copyright. For selected photographs only, the organisers and the City of Cluses receive a free, non-exclusive five-year permission covering the results, the exhibition, the catalogue and promotion.
The contest is open to amateur, semi-professional and professional photographers of any nationality aged 18 or over. Entries close on 30 November 2026 at 23:59 Paris time, and results are announced on 21 December 2026. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free (2 photos); €5 / €10 / €15 for 3 / 10 / 20 paid photos, +€2 each after. Prize: Exhibition at Images & Neige, Cluses (7 winners, production covered) + 22 category prizes.

item.title: Beyond Borders — International Photography Exhibition · iTravelPoetry
item.description: A three-city touring photography exhibition from iTravelPoetry, an independent Greek cultural organisation that runs a cultural venue in Chalandri, Athens, alongside a poetry competition, a film festival and publications. Its first photography festival closed with the group show "Within the Frame" at that venue in October 2026. Beyond Borders asks photographers to work with borders of any kind — geographical, cultural, social, emotional or entirely personal — or to challenge the idea of a border altogether; every genre and technique is welcome, from documentary and street to conceptual and experimental. Open to photographers aged 18 and over of any nationality, experience or background, with up to three images per applicant submitted by email as JPGs with titles. Read the cost carefully before applying: applying is free, but a €150 participation fee is charged to photographers whose work is selected and who then confirm their place, covering all three cities with no per-city extra. Selected photographs are shown in Athens, Paris and Rome, but the organisers state that exhibition dates and venue details will only be announced after submissions close, and no jury, prize or sales terms are published. Submissions run 17 October to 30 November 2026. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free (€150 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: KG+ 2027 Open Call · KYOTOGRAPHIE
item.description: KG+ is the satellite programme of the KYOTOGRAPHIE International Photography Festival, launched in 2013 to discover and support emerging artists and curators; 2027 is its fifteenth edition. Applicants propose a solo or group exhibition of photography — or of work incorporating photographic elements, including moving image and installation — to be staged at a venue in Kyoto City during the festival, 17 April to 16 May 2027. Applications are open regardless of age, profession, nationality or experience, but applicants must secure their own venue before applying and submit a signed venue usage permission form; the exhibition must be open to the public for at least nine days of the festival period, at least one of them a weekend or Japanese national holiday. Selected exhibitions enter the official KG+ programme in one of two categories (KG+ PICK UP or KG+), are published on the festival website and map, receive free promotional signage, and are eligible for discounted KYOTOGRAPHIE masterclasses and portfolio reviews, as well as the KG+ Discovery Award. The application fee is JPY 18,000, non-refundable, and includes one KYOTOGRAPHIE 2027 Passport. Note that participants bear all exhibition costs themselves — venue rental, printing, framing, transport, installation and deinstallation. Applications close 31 December 2026 at 23:59 JST; applicants are notified by late January 2027, and those who apply by 30 November 2026 hear by the end of 2026. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: ¥18,000 (incl. festival passport). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Weir Farm Artist-in-Residence Program
item.description:
A one-month residency on the 68-acre Weir Farm National Historical Park in Wilton, Connecticut, continuing "the creative legacy of Julian Alden Weir by supporting contemporary artists whose work advances artistic dialogue and innovation." Over 250 artists have taken part; the park's enabling legislation "underscores the importance of maintaining an active artistic presence," and the programme is framed as fostering "contemporary visual art practices that engage with and interpret the world in creative, experimental, and thought-provoking ways." One artist is in residence at a time, for four weeks between May and October 2027.
Photography is named explicitly: applicants "may apply in any of the following visual art media: Painting, Photography, Printmaking, Sculpture, Fiber Art, Mixed Media," and the park "encourages applications from artists representing a wide range of perspectives and media." Housing and studio space are provided — a fully furnished historic residence in the middle of the park, and the AIR Studio a few steps away, built in 2010 on the footprint of the former garage and awarded the NPS Certificate of Honor. Artists receive a $400 stipend, $200 at the start and $200 after the residency on completion of the requirements. Artists supply their own food, personal items and art supplies and provide their own transportation to and from the park, and the park warns the site "is very quiet and dark at night."
On accessibility: the programme "welcomes artists of all physical capabilities"; the art studio and restroom are wheelchair accessible, the historic cottage is not, and artists are not required to stay in the cottage, though off-site accommodation is at their own expense.
Open to US citizens and permanent residents aged 25 or over who are graduate students, emerging or professional artists, applying as individuals — couples and collectives are not considered. Anyone who held a residency between 2017 and 2026 is ineligible for the 2027 cohort. Residents must commit to the full four weeks, attend a welcome event, present a public Open Studio on the last Saturday of the residency, send 3–5 images mid-residency for social media, and take part in a recorded Zoom interview. Outdoor installations, open flame, kilns, toxic or hazardous materials, collecting natural materials on federal land and selling work on site are all prohibited.
A three-member jury drawn from academia, museums, galleries, professional artists and former residents weighs artistic merit, a well-defined and realistic project proposal, the answer to the "Why Weir Farm" question, and the artist's ability to commit. All applicants are notified by mid-March 2027. The programme is supported by the Friends of Weir Farm NHP, with a 2027 grant from the Connecticut company Tauck. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: $35. Prize: $400 stipend + Residency (1 month).

item.title: Elemental · Artspiration Frederick
item.description:
"Earth. Water. Air. Fire." A juried exhibition at Artspiration Frederick "where artists explore these powerful forces of nature and the ways they intersect with materiality, imagination, and the human experience." Artists are encouraged to interpret the elements "literally, symbolically, or abstractly, exploring themes of transformation, resilience, movement, balance, and change", and — working across all mediums — to consider "not only the elements themselves, but also the physical properties of their materials and the processes through which their work takes shape." The gallery says it welcomes "innovative and thought-provoking interpretations that reveal the extraordinary possibilities found within nature's most fundamental forces."
All media are accepted and photography is named among them. Up to three exhibition-ready works may be submitted and up to three may be selected, each needing a 300 dpi image for jurying; 2D work must be framed with a wire for hanging (no sawtooth hangers). Open to visual artists 18 and over residing in the continental US. The show runs 2–25 April 2027 at 915 Toll House Ave in Frederick, with an opening reception on 10 April, free and open to the public. Accepted work is dropped off 28–30 March or shipped to arrive by 30 March at the artist's cost, with a return label included, and retrieved by 10 May.
All work must be for sale and the gallery retains 40% of the sale price, the artist 60%. Prices are locked at entry — the gallery will not accept price changes once a piece has been submitted.
The juror is Lisa Sheirer, who has a BFA in painting and printmaking from West Virginia University and an MFA in sculpture from Notre Dame, works in "pixels, clay, ink, paint, wood, and sound", and is an artist in residence at the Ausherman Y Arts Center in downtown Frederick. Her public work includes a ceramic mural at Baltimore-Washington International Airport for the Maryland Department of Transportation and a glass mural at UPMC Western Maryland Hospital; she self-published the artist book "WaterShed" in 2023 with an NEA/Frederick Arts Council grant and holds the Jean Royer Kohr Memorial Lectureship. One term to read before shipping: the artist must retrieve all work no later than 10 May 2027, and work not collected within fourteen calendar days of the agreed pick-up date "shall incur a storage fee of Fifty Dollars ($50.00) until removed", with the gallery free to relocate it at the artist’s expense and risk. — Deadline: March 12, 2027. Fee: $35 ($25 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SO THEY SAY — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
item.description:
A public art exhibition on bus shelter ad space in Miami, opening 30 December 2026 and curated by Katelyn Kopenhaver. The brief turns the medium on itself: "Advertising follows us everywhere. From our phones to the streets, it appears on screens floating in the ocean or hovering above our heads. We are constantly being sold something: a product, a belief, an emotion, or an idea of who we should aspire to be. These messages seep into our subconscious, shaping our perceptions and sense of identity, often without question or consent."
SaveArtSpace asks for work "specifically conceived for the bus shelter, rather than treating it as an alternative gallery wall" — "operating within the very infrastructure it seeks to examine". Through humour and/or critical inquiry, artists are encouraged to engage with the mechanics of advertising, "playing with expectations and turning a space designed to persuade us into one that questions what we're being told."
Open to "artists of all ages and talents". Up to 10 JPEGs, each a maximum of 2 MB; selected artists are asked for high-resolution files afterwards. Selected artists are announced after 7 December 2026 and the work goes up on Miami bus shelter ad space from 30 December for at least one month. Fees are framed as tax-deductible donations that buy the ad space itself. The organiser’s FAQ adds that anyone who cannot afford the donation may submit their work by email instead, with the name of the open call as the subject.
The curator, Katelyn Kopenhaver (b. 1992), took a BFA in Photography from the School of Visual Arts and works across public intervention, performance, text and lens-based media; she is a studio resident at Bakehouse Art Complex in Miami, a NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellow (2021) and a Miami Individual Artist Grant recipient (2024 and 2026), and appeared in Der Greif Issue 18 curated by Hank Willis Thomas. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images) + $10 each additional ($36.92–$108.45 at checkout). Prize: Bus shelter exhibition in Miami.

item.title: Persistence of Memory · A Photographer's Place
item.description:
A monthly juried show in Gallery X at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, built on the question "If the past is never entirely gone, what remains?" The gallery invites photographic artists to submit work for an exhibition "examining the complex and often elusive relationship between memory, time, and perception", noting that while "a photograph can preserve a fleeting moment, but memory is far less predictable. It distorts, reconstructs, conceals, and reveals."
The call seeks "images that consider what remains after the moment has passed" — the imprint of a person, the familiarity of a place, the weight of history, the passage of time, or the fragments of an experience that refuse to fade. Interpretations that are personal, historical, psychological, conceptual, poetic or experimental are all encouraged, as is work exploring remembrance and forgetting, nostalgia and displacement, identity and transformation, or "the blurred boundaries between what is real and what is remembered". Selection weighs relevance to the theme, technical quality and originality, and artistic vision and storytelling.
Selected work hangs in Gallery X at the front of the space from 4 December 2026 to 2 January 2027, with an opening reception on 4 December, and is then presented on the gallery's website to be viewed year-round. Up to 5 JPEGs, colour or black and white, minimum 3000 pixels on the longest side; work must be delivered to the gallery by 2 December. Accepted artists may optionally have their work printed by the gallery on its Canon imagePROGRAF PRO-1100. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 5 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibit Your Work — Exhibition Proposals · Photosynthesis NZ
item.description:
Photosynthesis, the volunteer-run photography gallery, darkroom and studio on Battersea Street in Sydenham, Ōtautahi Christchurch, takes exhibition proposals all year through an expression-of-interest form. Its exhibitions run in sponsored seasons of ten weeks at no cost to the exhibitors, with one or two shows on at a time, each for two or three weeks.
